Slow to begin.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Apprentice E C W Wong pleaded guilty to a careless riding charge for causing interference near the 300 Metres (see CASA LEGEND).  Inside the final 100 Metres shifted out under pressure whilst being ridden along, inconveniencing GALE SAGA.  Apprentice E C W Wong explained that his instructions were to take up a more forward position but was left with  no alternative than to ride his mount back after missing the start.  Sent for sampling post-race.

Near the 200 Metres K Teetan had his whip knocked from his grasp by the whip of Apprentice E C W Wong (WINNING MACHINE).  Inconvenienced after passing the 100 Metres by WINNING MACHINE which shifted out.
Shortly after the start got its head up.  Held up after passing the 400 Metres until inside the 200 Metres.
Was unable to improve its position from the 500 Metres and was then held up for clear running from the 400 Metres until inside the 300 Metres.
No report.
C L Chau was severely reprimanded in relation to using his whip in a manner where the hand holding the whip was above shoulder height on three occasions between the 200 Metres and the 150 Metres.
Held up after passing the 400 Metres and failed to obtain clear running until inside the 100 Metres.
D Probert advised that his instructions were to ride his mount more quietly today which was confirmed by Trainer K W Lui.
On jumping shifted out and bumped SPEEDY TRIDENT.
On jumping got unbalanced when bumped by EURO ROCKS which shifted out.

Slow to begin.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Apprentice E C W Wong (WINNING MACHINE) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that near the 300 Metres he permitted his mount to shift out when insufficiently clear of CASA LEGEND, resulting in CASA LEGEND having to be checked and in doing so having to avoid the heels of GALE SAGA.  Apprentice Wong was suspended from riding in races for a period to commence on Wednesday, 11 March 2026 and to expire on Thursday, 19 March 2026 on which day he may resume race riding (3 Hong Kong racedays).  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his poor race riding record.
Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event. M L Yeung was warned for using his whip forward of the saddle in a forehand manner on one occasion near the 250 Metres.

L Ferraris reported that his instructions were to take up a forward position if not lead.  Trainer B Crawford confirmed the instructions issued as GOOD PROSPECT failed to quicken when ridden back at its last start, therefore they decided to go forward today.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

After passing the 300 Metres was disappointed for clear running between NATURAL HIGH and GLACIATED before shifting back to the inside of NATURAL HIGH to obtain clear running passing the 200 Metres.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Shifted out under pressure over the concluding stages, obliging its rider to stop riding and straighten.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Slow to begin.  Raced very wide and without cover from the 600 Metres.
Shifted out when negotiating the turn near the 700 Metres, making contact with the hindquarters of NATURAL HIGH.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Stumbled out of the barriers.
No report.
Rounding the turn near the 700 Metres got unbalanced after being bumped on the hindquarters by MR COOL which shifted out.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.

Slow to begin and then a short distance later was checked when crowded for room between KING DANCE which shifted in slightly and SMILING CHAMPION which jumped awkwardly and shifted out after being taken out slightly by LUCKY XANDER.  R Kingscote reported that the pre-race plans were to take up a forward position, however, was unable to do so after the incident at the start.

Near the 700 Metres was eased to avoid the heels of HINOKAMI KAGURA which also was eased to avoid the heels of HERBAL STAR which shifted in when laying in despite the efforts of its rider M Guyon.  In all the circumstances no further action was taken.  A Badel reported that his mount travelled well in the early stages, however, after suffering interference near the 700 Metres his mount failed to travel well after that.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Near the 700 Metres was eased to avoid the heels of HERBAL STAR which shifted in when not fully clear.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Jumped awkwardly.

K Teetan was advised to exercise more care when allowing his mount to shift out over the concluding stages whilst riding it along with the whip and in doing so inconveniencing ONE MAN SHOW and JUICY DRAGON by taking both runners wider.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Crowded soon after the start.  Taken wider over the concluding stages by SPEEDY SMARTIE which shifted out.

Approaching the 300 Metres became unbalanced when bumped by ONE MAN SHOW which was being shifted to the outside of SPEEDY SMARTIE to improve.  Taken wider over the concluding stages by ONE MAN SHOW which was taken out by SPEEDY SMARTIE.  As a result C Y Ho was unable to ride his mount out fully to the winning post when awkwardly placed on the heels of GOOD CHAP.
No report.

A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Nevertheless M L Yeung was advised to exercise more  care to prevent his mounts from shifting ground when they are under pressure.

Slow to begin.  When questioned L Hewitson stated that whilst he had an uninterrupted run in the Home Straight he was hesitant to take a run to the inside of MONEY CATCHER approaching the 200 Metres until he was satisfied there was clear running to do so.
K C Leung reported that it was not his intention to lead but was left with no alternative in the early stages when the pace was slow and to avoid racing wide and without cover.
SMART AVENUE, which was racing very wide, commenced a forward move after passing the 900 Metres to gain a position outside the leader near the 700 Metres to avoid covering excessive ground.
Passing the 900 Metres shifted out when over-racing, forcing SUPREME MASTERMIND wide.
Failed to obtain clear running in the Home Straight and subsequently was unable to be tested to the line.

Approaching the 200 Metres was held up for clear running, was checked and shifted out to avoid the heels of SMART AVENUE.  AERODYNAMICS continued to have difficulty obtaining clear running before being checked again over the concluding stages after failing to obtain a run between SMART AVENUE and THE AUSPICIOUS.
Passing the 900 Metres was bumped and shifted out by STUNNING PEACH which was over-racing, resulting in SUPREME MASTERMIND racing very wide and without cover.

Hung out rounding the Home Turn.  When questioned C Y Ho explained that the overall performance, in his opinion, was due to his mount being obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event and was disadvantaged by the slow early pace.  He further explained that from the 1000 Metres he was reluctant to go forward and take up a position outside the lead when SMART AVENUE had commenced a similar move and felt that it would be detrimental to his mount’s chances even more if he had done so.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Trainer W Y So advised that the horse would be ridden more quietly today as compared to its last start.
